edges.description: More severe forebrain non-separation is associated with more severe neurologic dysfunction.
Failed forebrain cleavage can include the deep gray nuclei, producing incomplete separation of the caudate and lentiform nuclei.
The forebrain midline developmental defect can involve formation of the olfactory apparatus, leaving absent olfactory bulbs.
Failure of midline cleavage extends to the hypothalamic nuclei.
Brain midline defects disrupt pituitary gland formation, causing endocrine insufficiency.
The failed cleavage of the prosencephalon is, viewed clinically and radiologically, the holoprosencephaly phenotype itself.
Complete or near-complete failure of hemispheric separation produces the alobar subtype, the severe end of the continuum.
Partial posterior separation with persistent anterior fusion produces the semilobar subtype.
Near-complete separation with residual frontal midline continuity produces the lobar subtype, the mildest structural grade.
The malformed, incompletely separated cortex is epileptogenic; cortical malformation predicts harder-to-control seizures.
Disturbed CSF dynamics in the malformed forebrain produce ventricular enlargement; a communicating dorsal cyst can accompany the malformation.
The malformed, volume-deficient forebrain commonly presents with congenital microcephaly (macrocephaly occurs instead when hydrocephalus supervenes).
Deficient midline facial field development narrows the interocular distance; hypotelorism is the hallmark mild-to-moderate expression.
Complete collapse of the midline facial field fuses the ocular fields into a single midline eye, the severe extreme seen with alobar HPE.
Failure of midline nasal field development replaces the nose with a tubular appendage at the severe end of the facial spectrum.
The mildest expression of the midline facial field deficiency: fusion of the maxillary incisor field into a single central tooth.
Impaired midline fusion of the facial prominences produces the characteristic median cleft lip-palate.
Overgrowth/fusion tendency of the midline nasal floor narrows the bony anterior nasal aperture in mild and microform disease.
Midline nasal airway maldevelopment in the microform spectrum also manifests as choanal narrowing or atresia.
Non-separated hypothalamic nuclei fail to support normal arginine-vasopressin production.
Non-separated hypothalamic nuclei also fail to support the non-endocrine homeostatic functions of the hypothalamus - circadian sleep-wake regulation, thermoregulation, and autonomic control.
The near-universal developmental disability of HPE is the developmental expression of the underlying neurologic impairment, with severity tracking malformation grade.
Cognitive impairment is a core manifestation of the neurologic dysfunction, most severe in alobar and semilobar disease.
Oromotor dysfunction from the neurologic impairment disrupts suck-swallow coordination, with poor nutrition and aspiration risk.
Anterior pituitary insufficiency manifesting as TSH-axis failure; identified in 11% of the endocrine cohort.
Anterior pituitary insufficiency manifesting as ACTH-axis failure (hypocorticism); identified in 7% of the endocrine cohort.
Anterior pituitary insufficiency manifesting as somatotropin deficiency; identified in 5% of the endocrine cohort.

Second-site modifiers act on the same hedgehog-dependent midline program as the primary SHH variant, shifting how far pathway output falls below the threshold required for midline patterning and thus where an individual lands on the microform-to-alobar spectrum.

edges.description: Absence of the olfactory bulbs and tracts disrupts the olfactory pathway and can produce loss of smell, including in HPE microforms.

The best-established non-genetic risk factor for this malformation, and one of the few exposures in this backfill whose intervening step is named by its own evidence rather than only by the entry's prose: periconceptional hyperglycaemia is proposed to act through oxidative stress in the neuroectoderm and cranial neural crest, converging on the midline field this node holds. That is why the intermediates are recorded as known.

Recorded as modulating rather than predisposing, and pointed at the variable-expressivity node rather than at a developmental step, because that is exactly what this exposure claims to do: it is not an insult in its own right but the proposition that a partially penetrant genetic lesion can be pushed past a threshold by an independent one. The cited sentence is candid that this is speculation and that what drives manifestation in genetically at-risk individuals remains unknown, which is why the grade is as low as it is.
